top_choice_rationale: P001 is an original experimental invention (Katori's magic-wavelength lattice, realised and pushed to the 1e-18 level by Ye's group) with quantitative performance verified across independent laboratories, and the credit maps cleanly onto two named people. The citation must name the magic-wavelength lattice to separate it from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes. P002 is highly original and opens a new door, but I cannot yet say the experimental credit is correctly identified (Cao, other groups, earlier continuum-model work) and the interpretation is still unsettled, so I rank it second. No award is last because a verified discovery is available.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile beyond collegial context: Goran Johansson is a Chalmers colleague, and Katori holds a University of Tokyo professorship where I have a long-standing microscopy exchange, but I have no research, financial or personal tie to Katori, Ye, MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero or Bistritzer.
